comment: Per-unit question inventory for the catalog. ONE ENTRY = ONE QUESTION AT ONE LENGTH (founder decision 2026-08-20): the 8-mark Section-C forms are their own LAQ entries, each SAQ entry opens its 4-mark answer, and no card ever shows two lengths. Source for SAQ/VSAQ: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024) pp.8-12 — question text and star rank only, never its prose. The book has no LAQ section for Unit 4; the two LAQ entries are the TSBIE Basic Learning Material Section-C forms of the same derivations, numbered here for the catalog. An entry without question_id renders as a coming-soon card. build_answer_book.ts hard-fails if an authored question is missing from this file or if a question_id/cut here resolves to nothing. Unit 5 (Laws of Motion) is the Fastrack's own pp.12-14 inventory, LAQ included: unlike Unit 4 the book HAS a Long Answer section here, and the TSBIE Basic Learning Material (pp.10-11) has NO Section-C for this unit at all — it runs VSAQ, SAQ, then straight into Unit 6 — so nothing sources a second 8-mark form and none is invented. Unit 5 SAQ 5 is the only entry in the book with printed exam years (May-12, Mar-04, 06). Unit 6 (Work Power Energy) is the Fastrack's pp.15-19 inventory, and here the TSBIE BLM AGREES on the 8-mark set: its Unit 6 carries exactly these three Long Answer questions and nothing else (no VSAQ section, no SAQ section), so the VSAQ/SAQ list is the Fastrack's alone. The opposite finding from Unit 5 — which is why the source check is per unit, not once. Unit 6 SAQ 1 is a CUT of LAQ 3, not a separate answer: one authored step list served at 8 marks and at 4. The book's PROBLEMS section (4 numericals after LAQ 3; the BLM repeats the first 2 as "Attached Problems") is DEFERRED, not dismissed (founder, 2026-08-20): a practice problem belongs to no paper section and carries no mark scheme, and holding one would need a 4th section value across the build, the player and the gates. Fastrack problem 3 does carry printed years "(Mar, May-14)", and the two books disagree on problem 2's answer (14.95 kW at g=9.8 vs 15 kW at g=10) — author them deliberately if they are ever added, never transcribe. BOARD-PATTERN STATUS (researched 2026-08-20, full analysis in docs/patterns/answer_book.md §Board landscape): the TS theory paper this book models stays 60 marks A/B/C for 2026-27 — the reform adds 15-mark first-year practicals outside the written paper — but the SYLLABUS is NCERT-revised for 2026-27 (new AI-in-Physics chapter, non-JEE/NEET cuts), so diff every unit inventory against the new TGBIE textbooks when they publish. AP diverged: 85-mark 4-section CBSE-style paper since March 2026, same NCERT question bank at different lengths (the 2026 AP paper asks several of our exact questions) — an AP edition is re-heading + re-cutting, not re-authoring. Unit 7 (System of Particles and Rotational Motion) is the first unit where the two-book check CHANGES the inventory: the TSBIE BLM carries two VSAQs the Fastrack lacks (the girl-carrying-bag centre-of-mass shift; two bodies with the same moment of inertia via KE = L squared over 2I) while the Fastrack carries six SAQs the BLM lacks (both axes theorems, the moment of inertia of a rod, and three numericals). Neither book is a superset of the other even inside one unit, so the inventory below is THE UNION - entries carry source: 'blm' where only the BLM lists them (no source = Fastrack). Both books agree Unit 7 has NO Long Answer section (the BLM runs VSAQ, SAQ, then straight into Unit 8's LAQs), so none is invented - the Unit 5 precedent. Entries with source: 'enumerated' are PREDICTED questions from the Session-89 enumeration sweep (archetype x object grid): never asked in any paper we know, authored as lean cards, labelled honestly in the catalog.

questions.text: State the parallelogram law of vectors. Derive an expression for the magnitude and direction of the resultant vector.
Show that the trajectory of a projectile is a parabola. Derive expressions for its time of flight, maximum height and horizontal range.
State the parallelogram law of vectors. Derive an expression for the magnitude and direction of the resultant vector.
Show that the maximum height and range of a projectile are u²sin²θ/2g and u²sin2θ/g respectively.
Define unit vector, null vector and position vector.
Show that the trajectory of an object thrown at an angle with the horizontal is a parabola.
Show that for a projectile launched at an angle of 45° the maximum height of the projectile is one quarter of the range.
If |a + b| = |a − b|, prove that the angle between a and b is 90°.

Two balls are projected from the same point in directions 30° and 60° with respect to the horizontal. What is the ratio of their initial velocities if they (a) attain the same height (b) have the same range?
Explain the terms average velocity and instantaneous velocity. When are they equal?
O is a point on the ground chosen as origin. A body first suffers a displacement of 10√2 m north-east, next 10 m north and finally 10√2 m north-west. How far is it from the origin?
The vertical component of a vector is equal to its horizontal component. What is the angle made by the vector with the x-axis?
A vector V makes an angle with the horizontal. The vector is rotated through an angle α. Does this rotation change the vector V?
Two forces of magnitudes 3 units and 5 units act at 60° with each other. What is the magnitude of their resultant?
A = i + j. What is the angle between the vector and the x-axis?
If P = 2i + 4j + 14k and Q = 4i + 4j + 10k, find the magnitude of P + Q.
Can a vector of magnitude zero have non-zero components?
What is the acceleration of a projectile at the top of its trajectory?
When two right-angled vectors of magnitude 7 units and 24 units combine, what is the magnitude of their resultant?

A man walks on a straight road from his home to a market 2.5 km away with a speed of 5 km/h. Finding the market closed, he instantly turns and walks back home with a speed of 7.5 km/h. What is (a) the magnitude of the average velocity and (b) the average speed of the man over the interval 0 to 50 min?
a) State Newton’s second law of motion. Hence derive F = ma from it. b) A body is moving along a circular path such that its speed always remains constant. Should there be a force acting on the body?
Define the terms momentum and impulse. State and explain the law of conservation of linear momentum. Give its examples.
Why are shock absorbers used in motor cycles and cars?
Explain the advantages and disadvantages of friction.
Mention the methods used to decrease friction.
Why is pulling the lawn roller preferred to pushing it?
State the laws of rolling friction.
What is inertia? What gives the measure of inertia?
When a bullet is fired from a gun, the gun gives a kick in the backward direction. Explain.
Why does a heavy rifle not recoil as strongly as a light rifle using the same cartridges?
If a bomb at rest explodes into two pieces, the pieces must travel in opposite directions. Explain.
Can the coefficient of friction be greater than one?
Why does a car with flattened tyres stop sooner than one with inflated tyres?
A horse has to pull harder during the start of the motion than later. Explain.
What happens to the coefficient of friction if the weight of the body is doubled?

A batsman hits back a ball straight in the direction of the bowler without changing its initial speed of 12 m/s. If the mass of the ball is 0.15 kg, determine the impulse imparted to the ball. (Assume linear motion of the ball.)
Calculate the time needed for a net force of 5 N to change the velocity of a 10 kg mass by 2 m/s.
State and prove the law of conservation of energy in the case of a freely falling body.
Develop the notions of work and kinetic energy and show that it leads to the work-energy theorem.
What are collisions? Explain the possible types of collisions. Develop the theory of one-dimensional elastic collision.

Show that in the case of a one-dimensional elastic collision, the relative velocity of approach of the two colliding bodies before collision is equal to the relative velocity of separation after collision.
What is potential energy? Derive an expression for the gravitational potential energy.
Distinguish between conservative and non-conservative forces with one example each.
State the conditions under which a force does no work.
Define work, power and energy. State their SI units.
State the relation between the kinetic energy and momentum of a body.

State the sign of the work done by a force in the following: a) work done by a man in lifting a bucket out of a well by means of a rope tied to the bucket; b) work done by the gravitational force in the same case.
Which physical quantity remains constant (i) in an elastic collision (ii) in an inelastic collision?
A body freely falling from a certain height h, after striking a smooth floor, rebounds and rises to a height h/2. What is the coefficient of restitution between the floor and the body?

units.name: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.text: a) State and prove the parallel axes theorem. b) For a thin flat circular disk, the radius of gyration about a diameter as axis is k. If the disk is cut along a diameter AB into two equal pieces, find the radius of gyration of each piece about AB.
Define vector product. Explain the properties of a vector product with two examples.
State and prove the perpendicular axes theorem.
State and prove the principle of conservation of angular momentum. Explain the principle with examples.
Distinguish between centre of mass and centre of gravity.
Define angular acceleration and torque. Establish the relation between angular acceleration and torque.
Define angular velocity. Derive v = rω.

Find the centre of mass of three particles at the vertices of an equilateral triangle. The masses of the particles are 100 g, 150 g and 200 g respectively. Each side of the equilateral triangle is 0.5 m long.
What is the moment of inertia of a rod of mass M and length L about an axis perpendicular to the rod and passing through one end?
The moment of inertia of a flywheel making 300 revolutions per minute is 0.3 kg·m². Find the torque required to bring it to rest in 20 s.
When 100 J of work is done on a flywheel, its angular velocity increases from 60 rpm to 180 rpm. What is the moment of inertia of the wheel?
Is it necessary that a mass should be present at the centre of mass of any system?
Why are spokes provided in a bicycle wheel?
By spinning eggs on a table top, how will you distinguish a hard-boiled egg from a raw egg?
Why should a helicopter necessarily have two propellers?
Why is it easier to balance a bicycle in motion?
We cannot open or close a door by applying force at the hinges. Why?
If the polar ice caps of the earth were to melt, what would be the effect on the length of the day?
Find the torque of the force 7i + 3j − 5k about the origin. The force acts on a particle whose position vector is i − j + k.
Why do we prefer a spanner of longer arm to a spanner of shorter arm?
What is the difference in the positions of a girl carrying a bag in one of her hands and another girl carrying a bag in each of her two hands?
Two rigid bodies have the same moment of inertia about their axes of symmetry. Which body will have the greater kinetic energy?
Define radius of gyration. Write its relation to the moment of inertia.
State the parallel axes theorem.
State the perpendicular axes theorem.
Define the angular momentum of a rigid body and write its relation to the angular velocity.
A ballet dancer spinning with her arms stretched folds her arms. What happens to her angular velocity?
What is a couple? Give one example.
State the conditions for the mechanical equilibrium of a rigid body.
Write the SI unit and dimensional formula of torque. Is torque the same physical quantity as work?
What is meant by mechanical equilibrium of a rigid body? State its conditions and explain what a couple is.
Define angular momentum. For a rigid body rotating about a fixed axis, derive L = Iω.
Obtain an expression for the kinetic energy of a body rolling without slipping.
